sourceDate.interpretation: Supplementary Hanshu volume 21, repository 023 s0278 explicitly dates the Grand Historian Sima Qian petition under Wu Yuanfeng seven; s0291 renames that year one, and Shiji 017 s2909/s2910 supplies the conventional BC 104 table label. Shiji 130 s0107/s0109/s0415 supports the existing author referent. This is his own official petition, not a date of reading or writing Rangju, nor the date when Ban Gu retrospectively narrated it. The source label is Yuanfeng 7, redesignated Taichu 1. The attestation is explicitly Hanshu-attributed, not an adjudication of variant reconstructions. Conventional historical year label only; a lunar year may cross Western-year boundaries. The calendar solstice and the fifth-month reform do not date this petition to a month/day. The 064 evidence IDs below identify the existing historian only; all numerical/event evidence is supplementary and pinned in references.json.

claims.event: Supplementary Hanshu-attributed personal office activity: Sima Qian, serving as Grand Historian, joins Gongsun Qing and Hu Sui in petitioning to correct the calendar in Yuanfeng 7 (renamed Taichu 1). Not his appointment date or the Rangju reading/composition date.

translationRepairs: Soldiers' encampments wells stoves food drink asked illness medicine, personally stroked and comforted them.
As for the soldiers' encampments, wells, stoves, food and drink, and inquiries about illness and medicine, he personally stroked and comforted them.

士卒次舍井灶飲食問疾醫藥，身自拊循之 is a topic–comment line: the welfare list is topicalized and 身自拊循之 means he personally stroked and comforted the soldiers; the before is ungrammatical telegraphic English, and the proposed after restores that structure without inventing or omitting sense.
All took general's provisions to feast soldiers, body shared rations equally with soldiers.
He took all the general's provisions to feast the soldiers, and personally shared the rations equally with the soldiers.

悉取將軍之資糧享士卒 means he took all the general's provisions to feast the soldiers (悉 modifies 取, not a plural subject), and 身與士卒平分糧食 means he personally shared rations equally with them; the before's 'All took' and calque 'body' are wrong, and the proposed after matches the Chinese.
Thereupon he beheaded the envoy's groom, the left outer horse of the chariot team, and the left outrider horse, and displayed the punishment before the three armies.
Thereupon he beheaded the envoy's driver, cut off the chariot's left upright, and killed the team's left outside horse, displaying the punishment before the three armies.

The Chinese enumerates the envoy's driver, the chariot's left upright, and the left outside horse. Suoyin explains fu as an exterior wooden support, separately from the horse, and connects the left side to the driver. The literal proposal restores all three objects, distinguishes cutting wood from killing, and retains the public punishment without adding a second horse or changing the actor.
Rangju thereupon beheaded the envoy's groom, the left outside horse of his chariot team, and the left trace horse, displaying the punishment before the three armies.
Rangju then had the envoy's driver beheaded, the chariot's left upright cut off, and the team's left outside horse killed, displaying the punishment before the three armies.

The continuing authority is Rangju; the envoy himself is spared in s0029 and returns in s0031. Suoyin distinguishes the wooden chariot upright from the single left outside horse. The idiomatic causative accurately expresses Rangju's ordered punishment, retains the driver's beheading and public display, and fixes the second-horse error without altering Chinese, chronology or identity.
